core_obligations: Record from the hypotheses that the two Koszul complexes are finite free resolutions of the corresponding quotients (proof lines 7648-7652).

Identify the Koszul complex of the juxtaposed sequence with the total complex of the tensor product of the two Koszul complexes and use the first hypothesis to replace one factor by the quotient (proof lines 7652-7660).
Recognise the result as the Koszul complex of the second sequence over that quotient (proof lines 7660-7664).
Use the second hypothesis to conclude that this complex resolves the quotient by all the elements, which is Koszul-regularity of the juxtaposed sequence (proof lines 7664-7669).
proof_roadmap: Read off the resolutions from the hypotheses (proof lines 7648-7652).
Tensor the Koszul complexes and use the first hypothesis (proof lines 7652-7660).
Identify with the Koszul complex over the quotient (proof lines 7660-7664).
Apply the second hypothesis and conclude (proof lines 7664-7670).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the Koszul-regular counterpart of the gluing statement for H1-regular sequences, and its proof is a 23-line chain of equalities and quasi-isomorphisms. It identifies the Koszul complex of the juxtaposed sequence with the total complex of the tensor product of the two Koszul complexes, uses the hypothesis that the first sequence is Koszul-regular to replace the first factor by the quotient, identifies the result with the Koszul complex of the second sequence over that quotient, and finally uses the second regularity hypothesis to recognise it as a resolution of the quotient by all the elements. Each of the four steps is attributed to a named statement, and the chain is displayed in full.
